learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Filters and Time Constants.
Apply Filters and Time Constants to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: High-pass, low-pass and notch filters attenuate selected frequencies. They can clarify recordings but also distort amplitude, phase and waveform shape.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Aggressive high-pass filtering can sharpen slow transients into false spikes; low-pass filtering can hide muscle or fast epileptiform activity. Raw data should remain available.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Understanding filters prevents false positives and false negatives in routine and quantitative EEG.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Using filters to “make the EEG look normal” undermines interpretation.

reviewPrompts.answer: Aggressive high-pass filtering can sharpen slow transients into false spikes; low-pass filtering can hide muscle or fast epileptiform activity. Raw data should remain available.
Understanding filters prevents false positives and false negatives in routine and quantitative EEG.
Using filters to “make the EEG look normal” undermines interpretation.
A cleaner trace is not automatically a truer trace.
